query: measured cost of methods for For each synchronized detection and depth pair, send through stage 2 only the pallet select_detection already chooses, and mark every other candidate deferred by publishing its source index on the pose diagnostics together with that pair's RGB and depth capture stamps. The handling process can then tell which pallets in the still-changing scene were detected but not posed.
findings: Posing every detection is the cost this method skips. CosyPose spent 190 ms of a 320 ms scene estimate on the 6D poses of all candidates (4 views, 6 detections per view, one coarse iteration and one refine iteration). Associating those candidates took 40 ms and scene refinement 90 ms (Labbé et al., ECCV 2020).

A pallet two-stage split shows the same imbalance. RF-DETR-S detection took about 21 ms and FoundationPose about 2.8 s per frame on an i9-9920X and an RTX 2080 Ti, so the pose stage is about 130 times the detector (scitepress 144556). Running that stage on the one box select_detection already chose is the saving. A whole-image pallet pose head does not offer it: YOLOX was 2.52 ms and the pose net 5.49 ms inside a 27.5 ms pipeline on an RTX 4090 (Miura et al., VISAPP 2026).

Per-instance second stages grow with the count that is deferred. EfficientPose reports that a detect-then-PnP runtime increases linearly with the number of objects, while its single-shot φ=0 model stays nearly flat: 27.45 FPS for one object and 26.22 FPS on Occlusion images that typically hold eight (Bukschat and Vetter, 2020). T6D-Direct is 0.017 s independent of instance count (58 fps, N=20 queries, RTX 3090). COPE is 0.075 s on the BOP timing and stays above 24 fps up to 90 instances, then slower than real-time, against CosyPose at 0.227 s and CDPNv2 at 1.010 s; at 15 instances it was about 7 times CosyPose and more than 12 times CDPNv2 (Thalhammer et al., WACV 2023). Deferring boxes saves a per-box refine or a per-box geometric fit. A constant-time multi-object head stays at that head's measured time.

A light shared second head is cheap even for many boxes. On COCO validation with ResNet-50 on a Titan Xp, Cascade R-CNN on an RPN measured 48 ms in the first stage and 78 ms total, so the later cascade stages added 30 ms at the default 1000 proposals (Zhou, Koltun, Krähenbühl, 2021, Table 1). The same cascade's proposal sweep, Table 6, ran in 66 ms at 1000 proposals, 48 ms at 256, and 42 ms at 64. Their probabilistic cascade, which already keeps 256 proposals, measured 47 ms in the first stage and 57 ms total. One selected pallet is that cut taken to a single box, which matters when stage 2 is a plane fit or a chamfer on that box.

One plane fit on a small face is a fraction of a frame, and each extra pallet pays it again. MRPT measured 0.5 ms for a 3D plane RANSAC on 300 inliers and 100 outliers on a Pentium M at 2.0 GHz. On a Jetson Nano in Python, sequential-probability-ratio RANSAC averaged 15 ms, converging in 8 to 57 iterations at a 5% failure rate (Zhuchenko et al., JEECS 2023). PCL plane segmentation on 120,000 points is the full-cloud version of that cost; Intel's AVX-512 rewrite of that step reports speedups from 10% to 300% versus the compared implementation. The selected detection's depth crop is the small instance of this fit.

Chamfer over a gallery is the expensive form of the same match. Liu et al. (CVPR 2010) recovered one object's 3D pose in 0.71 s with directional chamfer, against 29.1 s for chamfer matching and 65.3 s for oriented chamfer, by skipping most hypotheses. Classic chamfer was 17.59 µs per hypothesis on templates of about 1,610 points, and 1.05 million hypotheses took 0.42 s. Once select_detection has named the box, stage 2 scores that crop once. Each other candidate is an index on the diagnostics, not another search.

The deferred mark is a few key/value strings on the pose diagnostics already published for that synchronized pair: the source index plus that pair's RGB and depth capture stamps. Kronauer et al. (SenSys 2021) measured equal end-to-end latency at 128 B, 1 KB, and 10 KB, with the rise only at 100 KB and 500 KB once UDP fragments past 64 KB. An int32 index and two builtin_interfaces/Time stamps are 20 bytes before the key strings. Humble Fast-DDS 1:1 at a 4 KB buffer was 0.073 ms over UDP and 0.060 ms zero-copy (OSRF Sony report). For a 128 B payload, most of the time was DDS plus the rclcpp notification delay, and ROS 2 added up to 50% over raw DDS, so a second topic is another hop. The stock diagnostics channel is the slow hop for a scene that is still changing: REP-107 publishes DiagnosticArray at 1 Hz by default, and diagnostic_aggregator's pub_rate defaults to 1.0.

The sync that builds the pair can hold the frame longer than the index write. ApproximateTime with the default inter-message lower bound of 0 can delay a set by about one period T before it treats the match as optimal (ROS wiki). At 30 Hz that hold is about 33 ms. A realistic lower bound lets the set publish when the later of the two messages arrives. The stamps written with each deferred index are those two capture stamps.
